question: What is the primary focus of subjective data collection during a musculoskeletal assessment?

options.A: Checking laboratory test results for inflammation
options.B: Measuring exact joint angles with a goniometer
options.C: The patient's personal experience of symptoms
options.D: Testing deep tendon reflexes in the limbs

explanation: Subjective data relies on what the patient tells you about their pain, stiffness, and how symptoms affect their daily life. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h1)

question: Why do nurses ask about a patient's job or daily work during a bone and muscle assessment?

options.A: To identify repetitive physical movements that may cause injury
options.B: To check if they can afford prescribed orthopedic devices
options.C: To find out if they have health insurance coverage
options.D: To determine their exact monthly income for hospital billing

explanation: Work habits and daily physical tasks heavily influence joint and muscle strain over time. Great job thinking about the whole patient! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h1)

question: What is the correct order for examining a patient's bones, joints, and muscles?

options.A: Palpation, inspection, then range of motion
options.B: Range of motion, palpation, then inspection
options.C: Palpation, range of motion, then inspection
options.D: Inspection, palpation, then range of motion

explanation: Always look first (inspect), feel second (palpate), and test movement last. This stops you from causing extra pain before your exam is done! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h2)

question: A patient actively moves their arm through space without any nurse assistance. What type of movement is being tested?
explanation: Active range of motion occurs when the patient moves the joint entirely on their own power without outside assistance. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h2)

question: Which test is best for looking at soft tissues like a torn knee ligament?
explanation: MRI uses powerful magnets and radio waves to take clear pictures of soft tissues like ligaments and cartilage. X-rays are great for bones, but MRI wins for soft stuff! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h3)

question: A high level of uric acid in the blood is a major clue for doctors diagnosing which condition?
explanation: Gout happens when uric acid crystals build up in the joints. Checking blood uric acid is a fast way to spot it! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h3)

question: Which of these is a nursing diagnosis rather than a medical diagnosis?
explanation: Impaired physical mobility is a nursing diagnosis because it describes how the patient responds to a health issue, and nurses can independently help manage it. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h4)

question: A patient with a heavy leg cast reports a tingling sensation and toes that feel cold. Which nursing diagnosis is most urgent here?
explanation: Cold toes and tingling indicate compromised blood flow or nerve pressure, making neurovascular protection the highest priority. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h4)

question: How should a nurse touch a newly applied plaster cast while it is still wet?

options.A: With the palms of the hands to avoid indentations
options.B: With a heating pad wrapped tightly around it
options.C: With rigid metal clamps for support
options.D: With the fingertips to check for soft spots

explanation: Always use your palms! Using your fingertips can leave deep dents in wet plaster, which press into the skin and cause painful sores. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h5)

question: What is the golden rule for traction weights on a patient's bed?

options.A: Allow the weights to hang freely without touching the floor
options.B: Rest the weights on the bed frame to give the patient a break
options.C: Lift the weights manually during every nursing shift change
options.D: Disconnect the weights whenever the patient wants to turn

explanation: Weights must always hang freely in the air. If they touch the bed or floor, the pulling force stops working on the bone! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h5)

question: When is the best time to give pain medicine to a patient about to do physical therapy?

options.A: Only when the patient starts crying from severe pain
options.B: Immediately after the physical therapy session ends
options.C: Right before the patient goes to sleep at night
options.D: About thirty minutes before physical therapy begins

explanation: Giving meds early lets them kick in fully before therapy starts, helping your patient move with much less pain. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h6)

question: Getting patients out of bed early (early ambulation) mainly helps prevent which dangerous complication?
explanation: Walking contracts the leg muscles, pumping blood back to the heart and stopping dangerous blood clots from forming in the veins. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h6)

question: Why do nurses do an evaluation at the end of a care plan?

options.A: To determine if the patient met their health goals
options.B: To calculate the total cost of hospital supplies used
options.C: To assign blame if a complication occurs during recovery
options.D: To write a formal discharge report for insurance companies

explanation: Evaluation simply checks whether your nursing actions actually helped the patient reach their health targets. You're tracking success! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h7)

question: A home care nurse visits an elderly patient who just had a hip replacement. What is the most important safety tip to give them?

options.A: Remove loose throw rugs from all walkways
options.B: Keep all windows open wide for fresh air circulation
options.C: Paint all indoor stairs a bright neon color
options.D: Turn off all lights at night to save electrical energy

explanation: Loose rugs are a major trap for feet and frequently cause falls. Clearing the floor keeps your patient safe at home! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T21#GNS222_U1_T21_h7)
